tagline: Four computer-vision architectures, one cats-vs-dogs forecast—side by side in the browser.
short_description: An interactive comparison of HOG+SVM, a from-scratch CNN, MobileNet transfer learning, and DINOv2 probes, running client-side on ONNX Runtime Web with live holdout metrics.
long_description: fourcast puts four computer-vision paradigms on the same cats-vs-dogs task and lets you inspect where they agree and where they break. The Playground accepts a dragged or uploaded image (or a random holdout sample) and runs all four predictors in the browser: a HOG feature extractor with an SVM, a small convolutional network trained from scratch, a MobileNet transfer-learning head, and a linear probe over DINOv2 embeddings. Dedicated tabs expose the benchmark table and confusion behavior, the theory behind each paradigm, and the Rust/WASM inference code. Models are cached for instant startup, and the recorded holdout results show the expected spread—75% for the scratch CNN, 96.09% for MobileNet transfer learning, and 99.22% for the DINOv2 probe.
notes: Custom domain fourcast.livive.net from CNAME; GitHub Pages also serves the repo path. Ships a committed cats-vs-dogs holdout set with recorded metrics in data/all_model_metrics.json. The README is only a one-line summary; the site itself carries the benchmark and paradigm documentation.

how_to_play.title: 1. Pick a sample
how_to_play.body: Choose a holdout cat or dog, upload your own image, or hit Random Sample. The same pixels are fed to all four pipelines.

how_to_play.title: 2. Compare the forecasts
how_to_play.body: HOG+SVM, the scratch CNN, MobileNet transfer learning, and the DINOv2 probe each report a prediction and confidence. Watch the classical and foundation-model approaches diverge on hard crops.

how_to_play.title: 3. Read the evidence
how_to_play.body: Switch to Benchmarking & Metrics for the holdout table, Paradigm Theory for the trade-offs, and Rust / WASM Code to see the client-side inference implementation.
